audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6, First item and 2+ items all read 'Skill' while their own whys are explicit: whys[4] and whys[5] say Urgot-favoured, whys[6] says Dr. Mundo-favoured. The packet also flags the chart as contradicting the data.
audit.why: Urgot owns the lane from level 1 through his first item; the only stage Mundo takes is two items, which is where the 53% Emerald+ win rate is earned.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-6 and First item to Urgot, 2+ items to Dr. Mundo — matching the packet levelChart. Submitted as one atomic chart group across content win[] and full phases[].side/.rating.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4].why sold Level 6 as Mundo's flip and phases[5].why sold the first item as a Heartsteel spike, on a chart where both stages belong to Urgot. Neither said what the ultimates actually do.
audit.why: Fear Beyond Death is 100/85/70 at 2500 range and executes below a health threshold. Maximum Dosage instantly heals a percent of missing health on a flat 120s — which is exactly the interaction that matters here, because it can lift you back above the execute line mid-fight.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now states the impale range and the heal-over-the-threshold play; phases[5].why now carries Heart Zapper's real heal condition instead of a false spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Disdain was listed at 14 seconds — that is only its rank-5 value; it is 16s at rank 1 and 15s at rank 3, which is what you are tracking in lane. Its shield was never mentioned anywhere, despite being the thing that eats your commit. phases[2].why also claimed 'your passive shrugs the first CC', which is not something the data supports for a displacement.
audit.why: Riot text: Urgot charges in a direction, shielding himself, and hurls the first champion he catches. Cooldown 16/15.5/15/14.5/14, 475 range. Mundo's passive resists the first Immobilizing effect; whether a hurl counts is not answerable from these files, so no claim either way was written.
audit.corrected: Cooldown corrected to 15s at rank 3 in three places, the shield stated as the reason to force Disdain out before committing, and the unverifiable passive claim removed rather than replaced with a guess.

edits.before: Full kit online and your passive shrugs the first CC. Cleaver poke plus E-empowered swats start the grind; never brawl while Disdain (Flip) is up.
edits.after: Disdain shields him as he charges — 15s at rank 3, 475 range. Force it out before you commit or your Blunt Force burst lands on the shield.

edits.before: Maximum Dosage online — dives and all-ins flip when you press R mid-fight and regen half your HP. Force Urgot to commit, then out-last the commit.
edits.after: Fear Beyond Death impales at 2500 range and executes below a threshold. Maximum Dosage heals a percent of missing HP — press it to climb back over the line.

edits.before: Heartsteel timing — every proc widens the HP gap and your cleavers start hurting. Stand in the wave and dare Urgot to trade into the regen.
edits.after: His first item still out-damages your Heartsteel. Zapper only heals if its recast burst lands inside 325 — stand in him or you take the damage for free.

edits.before: Urgot-favoured: R execute turns your big HP pool against you.
edits.after: Urgot-favoured: Fear Beyond Death executes under the threshold.

edits.before: Force fights above the Fear Beyond Death execute threshold
edits.after: Press R to climb back over the Fear Beyond Death threshold

edits.before: - Urgot Disdain (Flip) (14s): matchup-defining — His engage. Bait it, then cleave. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
edits.after: - Urgot Disdain (Flip) (15s at rank 3): matchup-defining — his engage, and it shields him. Bait it, then cleave. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.

edits.before: Track Urgot’s Disdain (Flip) (14s): His engage. Bait it, then cleave. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Disdain (15s at rank 3): his engage, and it shields him. Bait it, then cleave — that cooldown is the green light.

edits.before: His windows: Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, Levels 4-5. Fight at your spikes, concede his — the level chart above is the trade calendar.
edits.after: His windows: Levels 1 through 6 and his first item. Yours is two items. Fight only at your spike — the chart above is the trade calendar.

edits.before: That spell is what punishes you — only step up once it’s down or baited.
edits.after: Disdain is 15s at rank 3 and it shields him — bait it, then commit.

notes: No mirror existed for this pair. UNVERIFIED and deliberately left in place: the entry asserts in four separate spots that Purge (W) deals percent-max-health damage ('%-HP Purge shreds your bulk', 'Stack %-max-HP items'). Riot's own description of Purge says only that he unloads his weapon on nearby enemies, and the kit file gives W a slow flag with no percentHealth flag — while Q, E and R all carry their flags correctly. I could not confirm or refute the percent-health claim from the kits, so I neither repeated nor removed it. If it is wrong it is load-bearing, because the whole win condition ('scale resists', 'stack pure HP is the exchange he wins') is built on it. Also unedited: diff reads 'FAV' while tone is red and breakdown.difficulty says 'Hard matchup — difficulty 8/10' against a 53% Mundo win rate — same inconsistency seen on the Teemo and Trundle entries, which suggests a template-level problem rather than a per-matchup one.
